page: Amazon Web Services c8i-flex.16xlarge is a compute-optimized server powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features 64 vCPUs and 32 physical cores utilizing the x86_64 Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor running at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz. The CPU architecture includes a 480 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for accelerated matrix and vector operations.

The instance is equipped with 128.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 7 GHz, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local NVMe storage, requiring network-attached storage options. Network connectivity is delivered via a baseline bandwidth of 15 Gbps.

In benchmark testing, the server demonstrates strong multi-core capabilities, achieving top-tier results in Geekbench multi-core execution, software compilation with Clang, and image processing. Its memory subsystem shows strong performance with cached read-only bandwidth reaching 5116.7 GB/sec. The hardware-assisted matrix extensions contribute to strong performance in LLM inference, particularly for prompt processing with medium-sized models, though large-model text generation represents a relative bottleneck.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c8i-flex.16xlarge offers a high-density compute profile with DDR5 memory speeds, making it highly effective for compute-heavy workloads without the overhead of local storage. It is well-suited for software compilation, high-throughput static web serving, database operations, and CPU-based machine learning inference.
